runs.label: Qwen 3.8 27B (0.32+MTP)
runs.gpu: 2 GPUs, --data-parallel-size 2 (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1). The 2026-08 runs used ONE GPU - normalise per GPU before comparing.
runs.bench_flags: vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --num-prompts 100 --backend vllm (endpoint_type=vllm -> /v1/completions; the 2026-08 runs used --backend openai)
runs.notes: PROVISIONAL n=1, and NOT a like-for-like comparison: this run used TWO GPUs (--data-parallel-size 2) where every 2026-08 run used one. Aggregate mean total tok/s 5,545 -> 8,329 (+50%), but per GPU that is -27% on average (-11% to -39%). Speculative decoding is on (method mtp, num_speculative_tokens 3; acceptance length 2.17-3.21, acceptance rate 39-74%), so TPOT is per accepted token and median ITL is per step: step time rose 25-43% while TPOT fell 41-64%. Prefill is ~1.9x faster in aggregate, which is roughly what DP=2 alone predicts. --kv-cache-dtype fp8 was dropped vs the 2026-08 config (KV bytes per token roughly double), and in-flight decode concurrency fell from ~84 to ~55 aggregate (~27 per DP rank); --max_num_seqs 969 rules out a sequence-count cap, so the limit is per-rank residency, not the scheduler knob. max_output_tokens_per_s in these files is broken (below average output_throughput in 13/16 files) and is not ingested.
